failures.criterion: Acceptance 5/6 and the Testing table: the three shell harnesses (up.test.sh, down.test.sh, checkpoints.test.sh) as the regression lock for the shell logic — their negative assertions must be able to fail
failures.evidence: Every bare `! grep …` / `! kill -0 …` line in the harnesses is a no-op under `set -euo pipefail`: bash exempts a `!`-inverted command from errexit (shellcheck SC2251 flags each: up.test.sh 164, 180, 186, 216, 227, 230, 238, 251, 265, 300, 313, 334, 339, 359, 379; down.test.sh 146, 147, 165, 178, 180; checkpoints.test.sh 269, 275, 331, 335). Proven three ways: `bash -euo pipefail -c 'echo canary >f; ! grep -Fq canary f; echo REACHED'` prints REACHED with exit 0; a copy of up.test.sh (in a fake repo root with the real deploy/ and packages/) with `echo "docker run --token anthropic-canary-value" >>"$FAKE_LOG"` planted immediately before line 180 still prints `refusals OK`, `host services OK`, `overlay and daemon OK`, `controller, bridge, root issues, summary OK`, `up.test.sh: OK`, exit 0; checkpoints.test.sh with `echo dispatch-secret-value-0123456789 >>"$tmp/out.txt"` planted before line 331 still prints `pod-hygiene OK` and `checkpoints.test.sh: OK`. The inert lines are exactly the ones that lock the security contract (a provider key never in an argv or stdout, the pod-hygiene FAILED output never carrying the token value, the kubeconfig never under ~/.kube/config, no tmux call on `controller: none`, down.sh's stopped processes actually dead). The guarded lines (`… || { echo …; exit 1; }` at up.test.sh 58/169/178/253/315 and checkpoints.test.sh 118) do work, and the live rig itself leaked nothing (sweep below), so this is an inert regression lock — a test that cannot fail hides an error — not a product leak. Fix in this PR: append `|| { echo '<what leaked>' >&2; exit 1; }` to each, or a `refute() { if "$@"; then echo "refute: $*" >&2; exit 1; fi; }` helper; the CI step `Test kind smoke harnesses` then guards what it claims to.

observations: LEGION-182 (filed by this tester): a root crashed while a worker's phase-complete was in flight never learns of it — daemon log 05:25:48Z `legion-demo-slegion26t-1-architect: receipt_timeout for event … on a live process; the holder is slow, not gone — nothing re-sent` five seconds after `resurrecting SLEGION26T-1`; the resumed architect's transcript ends at 05:25:52Z with `catchup-overseer snapshot: no new completions — retro still running… Parked for the retro wake`; the tree sat at `retro` with every worker retired for the next 31 minutes. The rig reported it truthfully as `kill-pod-resume FAILED: the tree … has not moved`.

The `architect shim connect for <KEY> failed (attempt k/6, cycle 1) … negotiate_protocol timed out after 5000ms` retry lines appeared after every root start on both instances, ending in `stopping architect shim connect … retries: the tree moved to generation 2` or the best-effort give-up — LEGION-39's documented ready-connect behaviour; /process/ready landed and the trees worked.
With the newer image (cli-v1.18.0, #1108 merged) under SMOKE_SESSION_STORE=pvc nothing changed: probe line `daemon-api-version=5`, every checkpoint as on cli-v1.17.0.

The checkpoints are lifecycle-sensitive: `architect-pod` asserts `in_progress` and `kill-pod-resume`'s mid-phase precondition (a worker holds a claim with a pod) is satisfied by idle finished workers too, so both are meaningful only when run right after `up.sh`/`tree-moved` as the runbook orders them. A one-sentence note in the README/runbook would spare an operator a 600 s wait and a confusing FAILED.

jq is a shell builtin in this OMP pane (`type jq` → builtin), which is why an `env -i` negative-control PATH built from `command -v` lost it; the rig's own `command -v jq` check behaved correctly in both environments.
documentationFeedback: Runbook and README are accurate for a run in the prescribed order. Two wording additions (fast-follow): (1) say that the `for c in …` loop and `kill-pod-resume` are meant to run right after `up.sh` — `architect-pod` requires the root still `in_progress`, and a kill during `retro` lands on an idle tree; (2) add the `architect shim connect … negotiate_protocol timed out` daemon-log lines to the troubleshooting table as expected (LEGION-39), since an operator reading the daemon log during a run sees them on every root start.
